name: strike-a-block
description: Browse a public vault of keepsake blocks and verify each one's SHA-256 proof of work. Read-only.

interface.longDescription:
Strike a Block keeps a public vault of keepsake blocks. Each block holds one line of someone's words (a dedication, a date, a name) and a SHA-256 proof of work: a hash that begins with a run of zeros, which is hard to produce and easy for anyone to check.

This plugin lets you explore that vault and check it for yourself, inside the conversation:

- Browse the vault. See public blocks as a grid of plates, newest first, and filter them by how many leading zeros their hash has.
- Show a block. Open any public block by its id to see its inscription, its hash and the 80-byte header the hash was computed from.
- Verify a block. Recompute the double SHA-256 of the header, compare it with the target stored in the header, and confirm that the inscription is committed inside the block. The view recomputes the hash again in your browser and stamps PASS or MISMATCH on its own evidence.

The plugin is read-only. It needs no account, keeps nothing you type and performs no transaction.

Good to know: the proof of work is computed on a Bitcoin mining chip, used purely as a SHA-256 engine. The blocks are standalone keepsakes. They are not on Bitcoin's blockchain, they are not a coin or token, and they have no monetary value. Inscriptions were written by the people who ordered them and are shown as written.
capabilities: Verify a block's proof of work
defaultPrompt: Show me the newest blocks in the Strike a Block vault.
Show Strike a Block block QQzyjAP6m9FXYLIgyKab.
Verify the proof of work of block YkAItiLPxhBf82KqhpWY.

positive.prompt: Show me the newest blocks in the Strike a Block vault.
positive.expected_behavior: Calls browse_vault with no filter and shows a grid of the most recent public blocks, newest first. Each plate shows the inscription, the number of leading zeros and the date. The text reply lists the same blocks with their ids and page links.

positive.prompt: Show me the 12-zero blocks in the Strike a Block vault.
positive.expected_behavior: Calls browse_vault with zeros=12 and shows only blocks whose hash begins with twelve zeros (five or more as of 12 November 2026), including the inscription "Twenty years married and I would still pick you first." The 12 chip is selected in the view.

positive.prompt: Show Strike a Block block QQzyjAP6m9FXYLIgyKab.
positive.expected_behavior: Calls show_block and shows the plate for that block: the inscription "Twenty years married and I would still pick you first.", a hash that begins 00000000000075d3 with tiles under its twelve leading zeros, and a proof panel that recomputes the hash and stamps PASS.

positive.description: Verify a block's proof of work
positive.prompt: Verify the proof of work of Strike a Block block YkAItiLPxhBf82KqhpWY.
positive.expected_behavior: Calls verify_block and reports PASS with four checks: the double SHA-256 of the 80-byte header equals the recorded hash (it begins 000000000000bb4d), the hash is at or below the target in the header, the merkle root matches the coinbase transaction, and the inscription is inside that transaction.

positive.description: Handle a block that does not exist
positive.prompt: Show Strike a Block block doesNotExist123.
positive.expected_behavior: Calls show_block, which returns an error saying no public block has the id doesNotExist123. The reply says the block was not found and suggests browsing the vault. It does not invent a block.

negative.description: Out of scope: creating or buying a block. The plugin is read-only and sells nothing, so it should say it cannot create a block or take a payment, and should not call a tool or start a purchase.
negative.prompt: Strike a new block that says "Happy birthday Sam" and charge my card.

negative.description: Out of scope: cryptocurrency actions. The plugin is not a wallet and its blocks are not on Bitcoin's blockchain, so it should decline and not call a tool.
negative.prompt: Send 0.01 BTC to bc1qexampleaddress and show me my wallet balance.

negative.description: Out of scope: changing the vault. Every tool is read-only, so it should explain that it cannot delete or edit a block and should not call a tool.
negative.prompt: Delete block QQzyjAP6m9FXYLIgyKab from the Strike a Block vault.

review.commerce_description: The plugin sells nothing and processes no payments. Its three tools read public records and verify them. It links only to public pages on strikeablock.com (a block's page and the vault), which is the site where the keepsakes are made and sold.

publication.release_notes: First release: browse the public vault, show a block, and verify a block's proof of work.
